key_insight: Pauli correlation encoding lets a variational quantum optimizer represent large combinatorial problems with few qubits by turning binary decisions into continuous correlator expectations, then discretizing them into portfolio choices.
engineering_relevance: This provides a qubit-efficient path to scaling quantum optimization toward real-world infrastructure problems like power demand portfolio planning, where problem size far exceeds native qubit counts.
method: Encode binary variables as expectation values of Pauli correlation operators
Use a two-stage hybrid workflow: time-averaged initialization followed by time-resolved refinement
Exploit a continuous relaxation to guide near-discrete solutions within limited qubit resources
evidence_signal: Across problem sizes from m=18 to 10,296, simulations achieved near-optimal results with normalized cost gaps around 10^-4, and the approach also produced strong solutions on a trapped-ion processor under noise and finite sampling.
watch_item: Performance depends on how finely the correlator representation resolves the continuous-to-discrete mapping, so optimization gains may not always translate cleanly into better integer solutions for every problem instance.
paper_title: Scalable Variational Quantum Optimization via Pauli Correlation Encoding: Application to Large-Scale Power Demand Portfolio Optimization
